## Glossary — Marketing & Attribution Terms

- [A/B Testing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/a-b-testing): A/B Testing, a cornerstone of performance marketing, is a methodical approach that compares two versions of a webpage or app to determine which one performs better. 
- [Active User](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/active-user): An Active user refers to an individual who interacts with a digital product, such as a website, app, or online platform, within a specific timeframe. 
- [Ad exchange](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-exchange): An ad exchange is a facilitator of buying and selling advertising inventory.
- [Ad inventory](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-inventory): Ad inventory is the available spaces for ads on a particular platform or medium.
- [Ad mediation](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-mediation): Ad mediation is a technology that allows multiple ad networks to be managed through a single SDK. Ad mediation platforms streamline the ad delivery process and maximize revenue, CPM, and fill rates for publishers. 
- [Ad monetization](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-monetization): Ad monetization generates revenue from advertising on a website or mobile app.
- [Ad network](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-network): An ad network serves as the intermediary between advertisers and publishers, helping advertisers land optimal ad inventories for their campaigns. This process is completed as ad networks aggregate available ad inventories from the supply-side (publishers) and match them with sources on the demand-side (advertisers) until they reach the targeted users. 
- [Ad podding](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-podding): Ad podding is when a group of ads are played back-to-back within a single ad break. Ad pods are used by OTT platforms that provide long-form VOD content. 
- [Ad server](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-server): An ad server is a technology platform that efficiently manages and delivers the most suitable ads to display in real-time. It serves as the central hub for overseeing and distributing ads across various websites, mobile apps, and other digital channels. 
- [Ad spend](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-spend): Ad spend is the total amount of money spent on advertising campaigns. Ad spend may indicate the simple cost invested in ads, or it may encompass extraneous costs from ad expenses, ad networks, etc. 
- [Ad stacking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-stacking): Ad stacking is a mobile ad fraud that places multiple ads on top of one another within a mobile app or web to inflate ad revenue artificially.
- [Ad tag](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-tag): An ad tag is a code snippet used to display and track advertisements on a website or mobile app.
- [Ad unit](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ad-unit): Ad units are the specific areas where advertisements are displayed on websites, mobile apps, and other digital platforms. Ad units come in various forms and are a useful monetization tool for marketers. 
- [AdTech](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/adtech): AdTech is a broad term that encompasses the tools and software used by advertisers, publishers and intermediaries to target, deliver, and analyze their digital advertising campaigns.
- [Advertisement](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/advertisement): An advertisement is a paid message designed to promote a product, service, or idea to a target audience through various media channels.
- [Advertiser](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/advertiser): An advertiser is someone that promotes a product or service with the use of advertisements. A mobile app advertiser promotes mobile apps to reach a specific target audience.
- [Advertising Waterfall](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/advertising-waterfall): Advertising Waterfall optimizes ad revenue by sequencing ad networks from the highest to the lowest yield and ensures that the most lucrative ad opportunities are tapped first, maximizing the potential earnings for publishers.
- [Analytics](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/analytics): Analytics refers to examining data to extract insights. Mobile analytics analyzes data from mobile devices to understand and improve the performance of mobile apps.
- [Android App Links](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/android-app-links): Android App Links are used only for Android devices and direct users to the specific in-app page when clicked.
- [API (Application Programming Interface)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/api-application-programming-interface): An API (Application Programming Interface) defines protocols and rules on how software programs should interact.
- [App monetization](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-monetization): App monetization refers to various ways that an app can generate revenue.
- [App stickiness](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-stickiness): App stickiness refers to the extent to which users continue to use an app after downloading it.
- [App store analytics](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-store-analytics): App store analytics is a marketing tool that provides app owners with a detailed analysis of their app’s performance, including key metrics that are essential for marketing growth. 
- [App store optimization (ASO)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-store-optimization-aso): App Store Optimization (ASO) is the process of optimizing a mobile app's visibility in app store search results to increase organic downloads and ultimately drive more revenue.
- [App tracking transparency (ATT)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-tracking-transparency-att): App Tracking Transparency (ATT) is a feature in iOS 14.5 that requires apps to obtain user permission before tracking their data across mobile apps, giving users more control over their data and increasing transparency around data collection practices.
- [app-ads.txt](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/app-ads-txt): Authorized Digital Seller for Mobile Apps, or app-ads.txt, is a text file that app developers/publishers upload on their developer website to control who participates in the ad-selling process. app-ads.text files include a list of approved ad tech vendors that are authorized to sell a publisher’s ad inventory for the purpose of preventing ad fraud.
- [Application (app)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/application-app): An application (app) is a software program designed to perform specific tasks on devices such as smartphones, tablets, or computers.
- [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/artificial-intelligence-ai): Artificial Intelligence (AI) is setting a new standard for efficiency and effectiveness in performance marketing and is used to help marketers predict consumer behavior, personalize advertising efforts, and enhance decision-making processes.
- [Attribution fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/attribution-fraud): Attribution fraud is a mobile ad fraud that claims credit for fake mobile app installs or in-app conversions.
- [Attribution modeling](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/attribution-modeling): Attribution modeling determines the effectiveness of different marketing touchpoints in driving conversions.
- [Attribution Window](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/attribution-window): Attribution Window is a timeframe within which the post-install in-app events can be attributed.
- [Average revenue per daily active user (ARPDAU)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/average-revenue-per-daily-active-user-arpdau): Average revenue per daily active user (ARPDAU) is a key performance indicator (KPI) that measures the average revenue an active user spends on a day on an app. It is used to evaluate the monetization performance of a mobile app. 
- [Average revenue per user (ARPU)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/average-revenue-per-user-arpu): Average revenue per user (ARPU) is a metric that calculates the revenue generated by a business per user over a specific period of time, typically a month or a quarter, by dividing the total revenue by the number of users or customers.
- [AVOD (Advertising-based video on demand)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/avod-advertising-based-video-on-demand): AVOD is a business model used in VOD platforms where viewers get access to the videos for free, in exchange for watching the advertisements included in the contents.
- [Benchmarking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/benchmarking): Benchmarking in marketing uses data to compare a company's strategies and performance against competitors to identify and implement improvements.
- [Beta Testing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/beta-testing): Beta Testing is a crucial phase where an app is distributed to a select audience to identify issues before its public release.
- [Bid request](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/bid-request): A bid request is a piece of code that enables the selling and delivery of display ads in real time. These codes are programmed so that when a user visits a web or app page, they connect to multiple programmatic networks to deliver user information and ensure that delivery systems fetch the most suitable ads open for bidding. 
- [Blocklist (Blacklist)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/blocklist-blacklist): A blocklist (also known as a blacklist) in the context of mobile ad fraud refers to a list of digital identifiers associated with fraudulent activity. It is used to block or flag suspicious activity in order to protect from potential ad fraud.
- [Bots](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/bots): Generally speaking, in marketing a bot refers to a software or application that is designed to automate certain tasks such as interacting with users. Bots can be used for various purposes to streamline marketing activities, but they are also exploited for malicious activities that interrupt marketers and damage brands. 
- [Branded link](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/branded-link): A branded link is a shortened URL that contains a custom or branded domain name instead of the original query strings. By replacing the long and unidentifiable URL with a memorable word or name, marketers are able to improve brand consistency and link click-through rates (CTR).
- [Broadcaster video on demand (BVOD) ](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/broadcaster-video-on-demand-bvod): Broadcaster video on demand (BVOD) is a type of VOD service that offers linear television content from traditional broadcasting channels. BVOD services are generally run by broadcasting networks and allow users on-demand access to previously aired shows or video content. 
- [Campaign Optimization](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/campaign-optimization): Campaign Optimization involves continuous testing, analysis, and refinement of campaign elements to improve outcomes.
- [Churn rate](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/churn-rate): Churn rate measures the number of users who stopped using the app over the total number of users in a given time frame.
- [Click farms ](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-farms): A click farm is an operation employing a large number of devices to repeatedly click on ads or engage with content, aiming to manipulate rankings, reputation, or search results. The goal is to distort engagement levels and artificially inflate an app, product, or service’s status. 
- [Click fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-fraud): Click fraud is ad fraud that intentionally inflates mobile app install or in-app event numbers by repeatedly clicking on ads or using automated scripts to create fake clicks.
- [Click hijacking ](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-hijacking): Click hijacking is an attack in which a user’s legitimate click is intercepted by some sort of fraudulent activity. By hijacking user activity and interrupting the original course of action of the legitimate click, attackers are able to trick users into performing other unwanted actions. 
- [Click injection](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-injection): Click injection is a mobile fraud that generates fake ad clicks with malicious software or script.
- [Click redirection](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-redirection): Click redirection (or automatic redirection) is the use of a script to redirect users who click on an ad to a different website or landing page than originally intended.
- [Click spam](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-spam): Click spamming involves the use of automated scripts or software programs that simulate fake clicks on ads.
- [Click to install time (CTIT)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-to-install-time-ctit): Click to install time, or CTIT, measures the time elapsed from the moment a user clicks on an ad to when the user installs and opens the respective app. This metric is often used by marketers to detect mobile ad fraud such as click spamming and click injections. 
- [Click validation](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-validation): Click validation is a mobile fraud prevention technique that requires ad partners to verify each click by matching it with its respective impression. In turn, marketers are able to detect fake clicks and prevent ad spend losses. 
- [Click-through rate (CTR)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/click-through-rate-ctr): Click-through rate (CTR) is a metric that measures the ad's ability and effectiveness in generating clicks.
- [Coarse Conversion Value](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/coarse-conversion-value): Coarse Conversion Value (CCV) is a metric used in the SKAdNetwork framework to measure and categorize the value of a user's action within an app in a broad or generalized manner.
- [Cohort](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cohort): A cohort is a segment of users that share a common trait.
- [Connected TV (CTV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/connected-tv-ctv): Connected TV (CTV) is a type of television that can connect to the internet and access online content and services.
- [Consent Management Platform (CMP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/consent-management-platform-cmp): A Consent Management Platform (CMP) helps businesses collect and manage user consent in compliance with global data protection laws, simplifying the process and improving user experience, operational efficiency, and responsible data management.
- [Conversion](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/conversion): Conversion refers to the desired end goal or outcome a marketer wants the users to reach based on the campaign’s objectives. 
- [Conversion Rate](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/conversion-rate): A conversion rate is the percentage of people who completed a desired action.
- [Conversion Tracking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/conversion-tracking): Conversion Tracking provides essential insights into user actions, from clicks to completed sales, directly impacting marketing strategies and ROI.
- [Cost aggregation](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-aggregation): Cost aggregation is the process of collecting cost data from various sources to create a unified view in ad spend.
- [Cost models](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-models): Cost models in digital advertising refer to the methods of charging advertisers for displaying or promoting their ads online, including CPM, CPC, CPA, CPI, and CPE.
- [Cost per action (CPA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-action-cpa): Cost per action (CPA) is a pricing model that pays for each specific action the users take after clicking on the ad.
- [Cost per click (CPC)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-click-cpc): Cost per click (CPC) is an ad pricing model where the advertiser pays the publisher each time a user clicks on an ad.
- [Cost per completed view (CPCV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-completed-view-cpcv): Cost per completed view, or CPCV, is a digital marketing pricing model that measures the cost of an online video advertisement that has a completed view. With the CPCV model, marketers have to pay when their video has been played in its entirety.
- [Cost per engagement (CPE)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-engagement-cpe): Cost per engagement (CPE) is an advertising pricing model in which marketers only pay for users that engage with an app in a specifically desired way post-installation. 
- [Cost per install (CPI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-install-cpi): Cost per install (CPI) is a metric that calculates the cost of acquiring a new user to a mobile app by dividing the total cost of a marketing campaign by the number of app installs resulting from that campaign.
- [Cost per mille (CPM)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-mille-cpm): Cost per mille (CPM) measures the cost of an ad per one thousand impressions.
- [Cost per view (CPV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cost-per-view-cpv): Cost per view (CPV) is a marketing pricing model where marketers pay every time a user watches their mobile video ad. 
- [CPA fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cpa-fraud): CPA fraud (cost per action fraud) is a ad fraud that occurs when a publisher is paid for fake actions.
- [Cross-device tracking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/cross-device-tracking): Cross-device tracking is tracking a user's activity across multiple devices by using various methods.
- [Crowd anonymity](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/crowd-anonymity): Crowd anonymity in SKAdNetwork acts as a safeguard for user privacy, setting the degree of confidentiality for an app user according to the volume of app installs produced during a campaign to acquire mobile users.
- [Custom Product Page (CPP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/custom-product-page-cpp): A Custom Product Page is a feature provided by the App Store that lets developers and marketers design distinct product pages with customized content, including screenshots, videos, and promotional text.
- [Daily Active Users (DAU)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/daily-active-users-dau): Daily active users (DAU) is a metric to measure how many unique users interacted with the app on a given day.
- [Dashboard](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/dashboard): A dashboard is a visual interface that consists of charts and graphs and provides an overview of key performance indicators and other important data.
- [Data Management Platform (DMP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/data-management-platform-dmp): A Data Management Platform (DMP) collects, organizes, and activates first, second, and third-party audience data from any source, including online, offline, mobile, and beyond.
- [Deep linking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/deep-linking): Deep linking can directly send users to a specific in-app content. It can build seamless user experiences across mobile web and app and be a powerful conversion booster.
- [Deferred deep linking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/deferred-deep-linking): Deferred deep linking directs the user to the in-app page after the app is downloaded and launched.
- [Demand-side platform (DSP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/demand-side-platform): A demand-side platform (DSP) is a software platform that enables advertisers to buy and manage ad inventory in real-time bidding auctions.
- [Device emulator](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/device-emulator): A device emulator is a software program that mimics another device's functions, enabling developers to test app functionality by simulating a device or an operating system.
- [Device ID](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/device-id): A device ID is a unique, anonymized combination of numbers and letters that is assigned to a specific device such as smartphones or tablets. It serves as a distinct identifier for each device, allowing it to be recognized and distinguished from all other mobile devices in the world.
- [Device ID reset fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/device-id-reset-fraud): Device ID reset fraud is a mobile fraud in which a fraudster resets the unique identifier of a mobile device to bypass fraud detection systems and use it for fraudulent activities such as creating fake accounts or making unauthorized purchases.
- [Differential privacy (DP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/differential-privacy-dp): Differential privacy (DP) is a way to protect the privacy of individuals while still getting valuable insights from the dataset.
- [Digital out-of-home (DOOH)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/digital-out-of-home-dooh): Digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising refers to the use of digital signage and screens to deliver ads in public spaces. DOOH ads are usually placed in high-traffic locations to drive awareness to a massive audience and bring an immersive experience. 
- [Dormant User](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/dormant-user): A Dormant User is someone who has downloaded an app and used it initially but then stopped engaging with it for an extended period.
- [Duplicate IP](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/duplicate-ip): Duplicate IP is a mobile ad fraud to artificially inflate app installs by generating multiple clicks and installs from the same IP address.
- [Dynamic Links](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/dynamic-links): Firebase Dynamic Links, offered by Google's Firebase platform, enables the creation of deep links that seamlessly guide users to specific content within your mobile app or website.
- [Dynamic product ad (DPA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/dynamic-product-ad-dpa): Dynamic Product Ads (DPAs) are personalized, programmatically generated ads that use consumer data to promote products to previously interested users.
- [E-commerce](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/e-commerce): E-commerce is short for electronic commerce and refers to buying and selling goods through the internet.
- [Earned Media](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/earned-media): Earned Media is essentially the recognition and visibility achieved through non-paid advertising methods. It is often achieved through word-of-mouth, social shares, press releases, and organic search engine results.
- [Effective cost per mille (eCPM)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/effective-cost-per-mille-ecpm): Effective cost per mille (eCPM) refers to the revenue generated by an app publisher for every 1,000 ad impressions served. eCPM allows publishers to understand the profitability of their ad inventory and find an estimate of their revenue.
- [Engagement](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/engagement): Mobile engagement refers to how much interaction and involvement a user has with an app or a brand through their mobile device.
- [Extract, transform, and load (ETL)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/extract-transform-and-load-etl): ETL refers to extracting data from multiple sources, transforming that data to be loaded in the system, and loading the data.
- [Fake users](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/fake-users): In marketing, fake users are accounts created by fraudsters for deceptive purposes. As the word itself states, these accounts are not used by real human users. Fake users are exploited for various fraudulent activities, typically to manipulate mobile marketing campaigns.
- [Fallback](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/fallback): Fallback acts as a safety net, allowing marketers to maintain engagement and tracking effectiveness even when primary methods encounter obstacles.
- [FAST TV](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/fast-tv): Free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST TV) is a streaming service that provides free access to TV shows, movies, and video content in exchange for watching ads in between scheduled breaks. FAST TV content can be streamed with internet connection instead of cable or satellite TV.
- [Fill rate](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/fill-rate): Fill rate refers to the percentage of ad requests that are successfully filled with ads. It is a crucial metric that reflects the effectiveness of ad inventory utilization.
- [GAID (Google Advertising ID)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/gaid-google-advertising-id): GAID is a unique and anonymous identifier used in Google’s advertising services to track ad performance and offer personalized ads.
- [Gametech](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/gametech): Gametech refers to the innovative technologies and tools that drive the growth and monetization of the gaming industry, particularly focusing on enhancing user engagement and optimizing performance marketing strategies.
- [Geofencing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/geofencing): Geofencing is a location-based service where an app uses GPS, RFID, Wi-Fi, or cellular data to trigger a specific action when a mobile device or RFID tag visits a virtual boundary.
- [Google Tag Manager (GTM)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/google-tag-manager-gtm): Google Tag Manager (GTM) is a powerful, free tool designed to simplify the process of managing and deploying marketing tags (snippets of code or tracking pixels) on your website or mobile app without having to modify the code.
- [Gross rating point (GRP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/gross-rating-point-grp): Gross Rating Point (GRP) is a measure of the size of an audience reached by a particular media campaign or advertisement, calculated by multiplying the percentage of a target audience reached by the frequency of an ad.
- [Identifier for vendor (IDFV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/identifier-for-vendor-idfv): Identifier for vendor (IDFV) is a unique alphanumeric code used as identifiers for iOS app developers. IDFVs are used to track user behavior across apps and facilitate cross-promotion activities.
- [IDFA (Identifier for Advertising)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/idfa-identifier-for-advertising): IDFA is a unique, anonymous identifier assigned to each iOS device for the purpose of tracking and targeting advertising.
- [Impression](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/impression): An impression is a metric in advertising that measures how many times an ad is shown to the audience.
- [Impression fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/impression-fraud): Impression fraud is a mobile ad fraud that creates fake ad views.
- [In-app bidding](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-app-bidding): In-app bidding is a programmatic advertising method where ad exchanges compete in real-time to serve an ad to a user.
- [In-app events](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-app-events): In-app events refer to actions or interactions that occur within a mobile application.
- [In-app header bidding](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-app-header-bidding): In-app header bidding is a programmatic mobile advertising technique in which multiple demand sources can compete simultaneously to bid for ad impressions. This technique differs from the traditional waterfall technique where bids are placed one at a time by going down the list of demand sources by ranking and waiting until an acceptable bid appears. 
- [In-app notifications](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-app-notifications): In-app notifications appear within a mobile app to provide users with relevant information, offers, or updates.
- [In-app purchase (IAP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-app-purchase-iap): An in-app purchase (IAP) allows users to purchase within the app for additional content or features.
- [In-game purchase](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-game-purchase): An in-game purchase is placed when a user of a mobile gaming app pays within the app to buy virtual goods like in-game currency, level upgrades, and new features. 
- [In-stream ads](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/in-stream-ads): In-stream ads are a dynamic form of digital advertising, placed directly within the content streams of videos, offering a seamless viewing experience.
- [Install](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/install): An install is the act of downloading and installing a mobile app on a device and is a metric used to measure the effectiveness of mobile app advertising campaigns.
- [Install fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/install-fraud): Install fraud is artificially inflating the number of mobile app installs through technical methods such as bots, fake accounts, and incentivized downloads, misleading advertisers.
- [Install hijacking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/install-hijacking): In mobile attribution, install hijacking refers to ad fraud where an attacker falsely attributes an app install to a legitimate advertising campaign to earn a fraudulent commission or inflate metrics.
- [Install referrer](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/install-referrer): An install referrer is an identifier to track the source of app installs of Android devices.
- [Instant apps](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/instant-apps): Instant apps allow users to access and use apps without installing them on their devices. They are limited to Android device users and Google Play Store branded apps only. 
- [Interstitial ad](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/interstitial-ad): An interstitial ad is a full-screen ad that appears between content pages within a mobile app or webpage.
- [IP Address](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ip-address): An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a distinctive numerical label assigned to each device connected to a network using the Internet Protocol, identifying its physical location.
- [K-factor](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/k-factor): In marketing, K-factor determines an app’s virality by measuring how many additional users an existing user brings to an app. K-factor is an essential metric for assessing the effectiveness of viral marketing campaigns and the organic growth potential of a product, service, or app. 
- [Key Performance Indicator (KPI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/key-performance-indicator-kpi): A KPI is a quantifiable measure to evaluate the success of an organization or a specific activity in which it engages.
- [Last Touch Attribution (LTA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/last-touch-attribution-lta): Last Touch Attribution credits the final customer interaction for conversion, offering a simplified view of marketing effectiveness.
- [Lifecycle tracking](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/lifecycle-tracking): Lifecycle tracking is a measurement of the stages an individual experiences throughout their lifetime as a user of a mobile app. By tracking the user journey, marketers can enhance their retargeting strategies and improve user retention. 
- [Lifetime value (LTV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/lifetime-value-ltv): Lifetime Value (LTV) predicts the profit attributed to the entire future relationship with a user.
- [Limit ad tracking (LAT)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/limit-ad-tracking-lat): Limit ad tracking (LAT) is a feature that allows users to choose not to receive personalized ads on iOS devices by opting out of having IDFA.
- [lockWindow](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/lockwindow): lockWindow in SKAdNetwork helps advertisers lock each of the three measurement windows sooner, thereby ending the measurement period earlier than the predefined schedule.
- [Lookback Window](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/lookback-window): A lookback window refers to the timeframe following an ad engagement such as ad click or view, during which subsequent app installs can be attributed to a specific ad.
- [M-commerce](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/m-commerce): M-commerce is short for mobile commerce and refers to buying and selling goods through mobile devices.
- [Machine Learning](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/machine-learning):  Machine Learning is the scientific study and construction of algorithms that can learn from and make predictions on data.
- [Marketing automation](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/marketing-automation): Marketing automation is a multifunctional technology that manages marketing activities with minimized human input. It can handle all sorts of tasks, from mass distributing emails to performing user data analytics in real-time, and streamlines the marketing management process for businesses. 
- [Mediation platform](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mediation-platform): Mediation platforms act as intermediaries between mobile apps, publishers, and ad networks, managing the relationship between supply and demand to serve the best-performing ads and maximize ad revenue.
- [Microtransaction](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/microtransaction): Microtransactions are small, low-value purchases made within games or apps, typically for virtual goods, upgrades, or digital content.
- [Mobile ad fraud](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mobile-ad-fraud): Mobile ad fraud refers to fraudulent activities on mobile devices using a variety of technology.
- [Mobile attribution](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mobile-attribution): Mobile attribution is the process of identifying and assigning credit to the different touchpoints that led to a mobile app conversion.
- [Mobile malware](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mobile-malware): Mobile malware is malicious software designed to attack mobile devices to gain unauthorized access, steal personal information, or perform other malicious actions.
- [Mobile marketing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mobile-marketing): Mobile marketing is the practice of promoting products or services through mobile devices in order to reach customers and provide them with relevant and personalized information.
- [Mobile measurement partner (MMP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mobile-measurement-partner-mmp): An MMP is a third-party attribution tool that empowers marketers to maximize mobile growth by measuring campaign performance across channels and ad networks
- [Monthly Active Users (MAU)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/monthly-active-users-mau): Monthly active users (MAU) is a metric to measure the number of unique users who engage with the app in a given month.
- [Multi-touch attribution (MTA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/multi-touch-attribution-mta): Multi-touch attribution (MTA) is an attribution model that calculates and distributes the conversion value to multiple touchpoints.
- [MVPD (Multichannel Video Programming Distributor)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/mvpd-multichannel-video-programming-distributor): MVPD is a company or a service that provides multiple channels through a wired or wireless communication network such as cable or satellite.
- [Native advertising](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/native-advertising): Native advertising blends in with the surrounding content to appear as a part of the publisher's website or app, providing a more seamless and natural experience for users.
- [Non-organic install (NOI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/non-organic-install-noi): Non-organic installs (NOIs) are app installs driven by specific marketing campaigns, such as ads or promotions on owned channels, which improve app visibility and lead to more organic installs.
- [OEM Advertising](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/oem-advertising): OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) Advertising is an emerging facet of performance marketing that targets users at the device level, leveraging pre-installed apps or software by the device manufacturers
- [Offerwall](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/offerwall): An offerwall is an in-app space that displays ads carrying some sort of task and rewards users in return for completing the task. It is widely used by marketers to monetize their app and increase user engagement. Offerwalls can be anything from watching a video ad to completing a survey within the app, and the reward can range from virtual currency to premium benefits. 
- [OpenRTB](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/openrtb): OpenRTB is a protocol that standardizes the process of bidding and transacting digital ad inventory in real-time between buyers and sellers. 
- [Organic install](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/organic-install): Organic installs are any app downloads that occur without the influence of paid or owned media sources like digital ads and campaigns.
- [OTT (Over The Top)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/ott-over-the-top): OTT (over-the-top) refers to the method of delivering content, such as video, audio, messages, and voice calls, via the internet.
- [Owned media](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/owned-media): Owned media is a marketing channel directly managed by a company, such as its app, website, blog, social media accounts, and email marketing campaigns.
- [Paid Media](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/paid-media): Paid media in performance marketing refers to any form of advertising that requires payment to place your brand in front of your target audience.
- [Paywall](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/paywall): A paywall is a digital barricade that limits a user’s access to certain features or content until they subscribe or pay for it. It is a monetization tool used by many subscription-based platforms to offer exclusive benefits and content to users who pay a fee. 
- [PC and Console](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/pc-and-console): PC and console advertising refers to creating and deploying ads specifically tailored to the distinct audiences and environments of PC and console gaming.
- [Phone farms](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/phone-farms): Phone farms are a collection of smartphones or mobile devices that are controlled remotely and used to perform automated tasks.
- [Postback](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/postback): Postback is the exchange of information between servers when an in-app event or app install occurs. It enables in-app activity tracking and carries data that measurement partners need for attributing installs and impressions.
- [Predictive Analytics](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/predictive-analytics): Predictive Analytics is a data-driven approach that forecasts future user behaviors, preferences, and trends by analyzing historical and current data.
- [Predictive lifetime value (pLTV)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/predictive-lifetime-value-pltv): Predictive lifetime value (pLTV) is a metric used to estimate the total value a user will generate for a brand over the entire duration of their relationship. pLTV uses machine learning models and artificial intelligence (AI) to conduct predictive analytics. 
- [Preferred deals](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/preferred-deals): Preferred deals are a type of programmatic advertising agreement that allows publishers to offer inventory to specific advertisers before making it available on the open market.
- [Premium video on demand (PVOD)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/premium-video-on-demand-pvod): Premium video on demand (PVOD) refers to a monetization model where OTT platforms provide viewers with early access to video content in exchange for a premium price. Unreleased movies or high-quality newly released productions are examples of exclusive content commonly distributed using the PVOD model. 
- [Privacy Manifest](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/privacy-manifest): Privacy manifests offer a novel approach for third-party SDK developers to disclose their data utilization and privacy protocols. This disclosure aids app developers in providing a precise depiction of privacy practices within their apps.
- [Privacy preserving technologies (PPTs)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/privacy-preserving-technologies-ppts): Privacy preserving technologies (PPTs) are methods used to protect the users' privacy while still allowing for the collection, storage, and analysis of data.
- [Privacy Sandbox](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/privacy-sandbox): The Privacy Sandbox is a groundbreaking initiative by Google designed to enhance privacy on the web and mobile by providing a set of open standards for digital advertising that do not rely on individual user tracking via GAID.
- [Private marketplace (PMP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/private-marketplace-pmp): A private marketplace in the digital advertising industry is an exclusive and secure platform connecting advertisers and publishers directly to buy and sell ad inventory, offering greater control, increased quality, and improved transparency.
- [Private set intersection (PSI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/privacy-set-intersection-psi): Private Set Intersection (PSI) is a privacy-preserving protocol that enables the calculation of the intersection of two private sets without revealing the individual elements in the sets.
- [Probabilistic modeling](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/probabilistic-modeling): Probabilistic modeling in MMPs is a method used to establish a causal link between ad exposure and a user's action, such as an app install or in-app purchase.
- [Programmatic advertising](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/programmatic-advertising): Programmatic advertising automates the buying, placement, and optimization of online advertising through real-time bidding and using demand-side platforms (DSPs) and supply-side platforms (SSPs).
- [Programmatic digital-out-of-home (pDOOH)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/programmatic-digital-out-of-home-pdooh): Programmatic digital-out-of-home (pDOOH) advertising refers to the automated buying, selling, and delivery of digital out-of-home (DOOH) ad inventory. It combines the benefits of DOOH advertising with programmatic transactions that enable precise and real-time targeting.
- [Programmatic Guaranteed](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/programmatic-guaranteed): Programmatic Guaranteed is a digital advertising buying process that allows advertisers to purchase a fixed amount of inventory from publishers at a set price, ensuring guaranteed ad placements and impressions.
- [Publisher](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/publisher): A publisher in digital advertising refers to a provider of advertising inventory.
- [Push notification](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/push-notification): Push notifications are a type of pop-up message on a mobile device sent to provide updates, offers, or other information to users.
- [Re-engagement](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/re-engagement): Re-engagement is the process of reconnecting with users who have previously downloaded an app but are no longer actively using it, with the goal of reigniting interest and encouraging continued engagement.
- [Real-time bidding (RTB)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/real-time-bidding-rtb): Real-time bidding (RTB) is a real-time auction process where advertisers bid on available ad space through a demand-side platform.
- [Receipt validation](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/receipt-validation): Receipt validation is an important process for mobile apps to ensure the authenticity of in-app purchases made within their apps.
- [Remarketing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/remarketing): Remarketing is a widely used marketing strategy that re-engages users who have previously interacted with a product/service or app. It is easier to target these users as they have already shown intent and are more likely to convert. 
- [Retargeting ad](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/retargeting-ad): Retargeting ads allow marketers to show ads to users who have previously interacted with their brand by using various tracking technologies.
- [Retention rate](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/retention-rate): Retention rates measure the percentage of users who continue to come back and use an app or service over a specified time.
- [Return On Ad Spend (ROAS)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/return-on-ad-spend-roas): Return on ad spend (ROAS) is a ratio that calculates the revenue generated for every dollar spent on advertising.
- [Return On Investment (ROI)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/return-on-investment-roi): Return on investment (ROI) is a metric to measure the profitability of an investment by dividing the net profit by the original cost of the investment, expressed as a percentage.
- [SDK spoofing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/sdk-spoofing): SDK spoofing is the creation of fake installs which can consume the advertising budget without actual value.
- [Search Engine Optimization (SEO)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/search-engine-optimization-seo): Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is the practice of enhancing a website-related content and structure to improve its visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs), driving organic traffic.
- [Self-attributing network (SAN)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/self-attributing-network-san): A self-attributing network (SAN) acts as both a publisher and an ad network and can advertise on its own platform.
- [Self-serve DSP](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/self-serve-dsp): A self-serve demand-side platform (DSP) is a marketing automation tool that enables marketers to fully manage and optimize the ad buying process in real-time. Marketers can receive direct access to ad inventory sources and control the parameters for ad delivery while everything else is automated.
- [Server-to-server (S2S)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/server-to-server-s2s): Server-to-server (S2S), also known as server-side tracking, is a method of collecting and sharing app or web data between servers. S2S is also how app owners communicate with mobile measurement partners (MMPs) and send event data in a secure way, without having to rely on the user browser and asking for tracking requests.
- [Session](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/session): A session refers to a time a user interacts with the app or website.
- [SKAdNetwork (SKAN)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/skadnetwork-skan): SKAdNetwork (SKAN) is a framework for mobile app install measurement and attribution on iOS.
- [Smart App Banner](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/smart-app-banner): These banners provide a seamless link between web content and mobile apps, encouraging website visitors to install or open the app. 
- [Soft Launch](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/soft-launch): A Soft Launch is the strategy of introducing a product to the market before its official release date, often with minimal marketing effort or publicity.
- [Software Development Kit (SDK)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/software-development-kit-sdk): A software development kit (SDK) is a set of tools that enables a developer to easily create applications for a specific platform.
- [Sub-publisher](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/sub-publisher): In marketing, a sub-publisher owns traffic that larger publishers buy and sell to advertisers. Advertisers only work with the network that trades with sub-publishers, not directly with the sub-publishers themselves.
- [Supply-side platform (SSP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/supply-side-platform-ssp): A supply-side platform (SSP) enables publishers to manage and monetize their ad space by selling it programmatically.
- [SVOD (Subscription-based video on demand)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/svod-subscription-based-video-on-demand): A subscription-based video on demand (SVOD) is a streaming service where users pay a subscription fee for the content.
- [Target Rating Point (TRP)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/target-rating-point-trp): Target Rating Point (TRP) is a metric to determine the percentage of the target audience that has been reached by a particular media campaign or advertisement, calculated by dividing the total impressions delivered by the total target audience, then multiplying the result by 100 to get a percentage.
- [Targeting](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/targeting): Targeting refers to identifying and reaching specific groups of audience by using data on characteristics like location, demographics, app history, and previous purchasing behavior. Marketers can use targeting to run targeted ads.
- [Temporary attribution](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/temporary-attribution): A temporary attribution model attributes credit of a conversion for a limited period of time.
- [Time of inactivity](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/time-of-inactivity): The time of inactivity is a metric that measures the amount of time that passes from when a user first engages with an app or mobile website until their next engagement.
- [Touchpoint](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/touchpoint): In marketing, a touchpoint is any point of interaction between potential users and brands. Touchpoints can be anything from online ad viewing to word-of-mouth communication. 
- [Tracking link](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/tracking-link): In marketing, a tracking link is a specialized URL used to report user activity on an app or webpage and understand traffic sources of marketing campaigns. It is also used to redirect users to other destinations and monitor attribution parameters. 
- [Tracking parameter](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/tracking-parameter): A tracking parameter is a value added to a URL to track the performance of a specific marketing campaign or advertising effort.
- [Transactional video on demand (TVOD) ](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/transactional-video-on-demand-tvod): Transactional video on demand (TVOD) is a monetization model where users pay for each individual video content they wish to rent or purchase. Rather than paying a subscription fee for platform-wide access, users pay on a per-title basis for streaming.
- [Uninstall](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/uninstall): An uninstall refers to deleting a previously installed app from a mobile device.
- [Universal links](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/universal-links): Universal links are deep links used in iOS devices that allows users to open a specific piece of content within an app.
- [Urchin tracking module (UTM)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/urchin-tracking-module-utm): An urchin tracking module (UTM) is a marketing analytics tool used to measure the performance of marketing campaigns. UTM parameters are the key pieces of data that enable the analysis and are added at the end of a URL. 
- [User Acceptance Testing (UAT)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/user-acceptance-testing-uat): User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is the final phase of the software testing process, where the end users test the software to ensure it meets their requirements and functions correctly in real-world scenarios.
- [User Acquisition (UA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/user-acquisition-ua): User acquisition (UA) is the process of attracting and converting new users to a product or service.
- [User loyalty](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/user-loyalty): In mobile marketing, user loyalty is when a user maintains an active and positive relationship with an app after installing and launching it for the first time. A user that drives engagement, repeat purchases, and overall contributes to the beneficial growth of an app is considered a loyal user.
- [User Stickiness](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/user-stickiness): User stickiness indicates how engaged and loyal users are to a mobile app over time. It essentially measures the app's ability to retain users and keep them coming back.
- [Video on demand (VOD)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/video-on-demand-vod): Video on demand (VOD) is a content distribution system that allows users to select and watch video content at their convenience without limitations to a specific device or broadcasting schedule. With VODs, users can access a wide range of content, from movies and TV shows to miscellaneous video content. 
- [View-through attribution (VTA)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/view-through-attribution-vta): View-through attribution (VTA) is a way to measure ad effectiveness by giving credit of a conversion to ad impressions.
- [View-through rate (VTR)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/view-through-rate-vtr): View-through rate (VTR) is a metric that measures the number of times an ad was viewed, divided by how many times the ad was shown.
- [Virtual multichannel video programming distributor (vMVPD)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/virtual-multichannel-video-programming-distributor-vmvpd): A virtual multichannel video programming distributor (vMVPD) is a streaming service that offers a bundle of live and on-demand linear television through an internet connection, without the need for cable or satellite TV providers. 
- [Walled garden](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/walled-garden): A walled garden is a platform where the publisher handles all the ad inventory and data.
- [Web attribution](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/web-attribution): Web attribution is to determine which source or channel of website traffic led to a conversion.
- [Weekly Active Users (WAU)](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/weekly-active-users-wau): Weekly active users (WAU) is a metric to measure how many unique users interacted with the app on a given week.
- [White-label DSP](https://www.airbridge.io/en/glossary/white-label-dsp): A white-label demand-side platform (DSP) is a fully-programmed software that businesses purchase and use to perform programmatic advertising. These DSPs come without a tag, and brands can rebrand and acquire the solution entirely once the transaction has been made with the developers.

## Do Any Mobile Attribution Platforms Offer a Real Free Trial?

## Why Most MMPs Don't Offer a True Free Trial

Mobile attribution is a high-stakes infrastructure decision. Once you integrate an SDK, switch costs are real. That's exactly why trying a platform with your own data matters, and why it's frustrating that most MMPs make it difficult.

A **free trial** gives you full access to a paid plan for a limited time. You get to test every feature with real data, real campaigns, and real attribution logic before deciding whether to pay.

## What Is an Official MMP? How to Check Any Attribution Tool

URL: https://www.airbridge.io/en/blog/official-mmp-partner-check
Language: English
Published: 2026-11-11
Author: Hyunjong Choi

**Short answer:** An official MMP (mobile measurement partner) is an attribution tool that an ad platform has admitted to its own measurement partner program. Google publishes its certified list. As of November 11, 2026, it has seven names: Adjust, Airbridge, AppsFlyer, Branch, Kochava, Singular and Tenjin. To check any tool, look it up on the ad platform's own list. Do not rely on the badge on the vendor's website.

**Why it matters:** Your ad budget follows your attribution numbers, and the ad platforms optimize on the conversions you send them. If your tool misses the platforms' own attribution data, or leaves the same install claimed by several platforms, you can move budget to the wrong channel and feed the platforms weaker signals. That is ad spend you may not get back.

## First, what does an MMP do?

Suppose you advertise your app on Google, Meta and TikTok. Someone sees all three ads and installs the app. Each platform may claim that install. Your reports can then show three installs, but you have one new user.

An MMP solves this. It is a third-party tool that sits between your app and your ad channels. It does three jobs:

1. **It decides which ad gets the credit.** It collects ad clicks and views from every channel, removes duplicates, and credits one channel by a fixed rule. This is called attribution.
2. **It sends results back to the ad platforms.** When a user installs or buys, the MMP tells the ad platform. This message is called a postback. The platform uses it to find more users like that one.
3. **It runs the shared plumbing.** This includes deep links (links that open a specific screen in your app) and SKAdNetwork reporting (Apple's privacy-safe way to report iOS installs).

Three terms appear often in this article:

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| **Attribution** | Deciding which ad led to an install or purchase |
| **Postback** | A message that tells an ad platform "this user converted" |
| **Self-attributing network (SAN)** | A large platform, such as Google, Meta, TikTok or Apple Ads, that decides inside its own system which conversions it claims |

## What makes an MMP "official"?

A logo on a vendor's website shows that some relationship with the platform exists. The program name tells you what kind. Four names are easy to mix up:

| Badge or status | What it is | What it takes | Is it about measurement? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Google Partner** | Google's program for companies that manage Google Ads accounts for clients | A 70% optimization score, $10,000 USD of ad spend in 90 days across managed accounts, and at least half of the account strategists certified in Google Ads | No |
| **Meta Tech Provider** | Meta's term for a business whose app needs access to data that other businesses own on Meta. It is an app classification, not a badge | Business verification, plus app review for advanced permissions, before the app can access other businesses' data | No |
| **Meta Business Partner badge** | A badge Meta gives to companies that meet its criteria | Criteria differ by solution type and weigh the amount and quality of work on Meta technologies | Not by itself. Ask which solution type the badge covers |
| **Google App Attribution Partner** | Google's certification for select mobile measurement partners | Google publishes no criteria. Its help page lists seven partners (November 2026) | **Yes** |

A Google Partner badge or a Meta Tech Provider status is not about measurement. Neither one is a measurement program.

TikTok works in a similar way. Its Marketing Partners directory shows each partner's category and specialty. For an attribution tool, look for the Measurement category and the Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) specialty.

When a vendor says "official partner", ask which program. Then find that program's public list.

## How do you check on Google?

Google's program is called **App Attribution Partner (AAP)**. Google describes it as third-party app analytics certification for select mobile measurement partners.

Google lists the certified partners on its help page. As of November 11, 2026:

- Adjust
- Airbridge
- AppsFlyer
- Branch
- Kochava
- Singular
- Tenjin

Check the current list on Google's page: [About tracking app conversions with an App Attribution Partner](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12961402).

Google names these benefits of the program:

- A streamlined integration between the tool and Google Ads.
- Early access to new measurement features.
- Fewer reporting differences between Google Ads and the tool, when conversion windows are aligned. A conversion window is the number of days after an ad click in which a conversion still counts.
- Easier import of app conversions into Google Ads.

## How do you check on Meta, TikTok and Apple Ads?

Each platform publishes its partners differently. Where a public directory or help page exists, the check takes three steps:

1. Open the platform's official partner directory or help center.
2. Search for the vendor's name.
3. Read which program the vendor is in. Measurement programs are separate from agency and creative programs.

If the claim appears only in the vendor's own marketing, treat it as unverified until you find it on the platform's side.

## What changes when your MMP is in the platform's program?

### Does the platform send attribution data back?

Google, Meta, TikTok and Apple Ads decide inside their own systems which installs they claim. An MMP with a self-attributing integration receives that platform's touchpoint data. Without one, a tool cannot receive it and relies on its own tracking links.

### Do postbacks improve ad targeting?

Ad platforms learn from the events you send them. Clear signals help the platform find people who will buy, not only people who will install.

In Airbridge, you set postback rules for each channel:

- **Which events to send.** Pick the events and map them to the channel's event names.
- **Attributed or all.** Send only the events credited to that channel, or all events.
- **First or every.** Send only the first event per device, or each one.
- **Value threshold.** Send only events above an amount you set, such as purchases over $20.

On the Core Plan, postbacks cover Google, Meta and TikTok with standard events. Apple Ads does not accept postbacks.

### Is one conversion counted once?

Yes. The MMP applies one rule to every channel. Three platforms may each claim the same user, and your MMP report still shows one conversion.

## Can a tool outside these programs still send events?

Yes. Any tool can send conversion events to an ad platform through public server-to-server or Conversions APIs. Google Ads also lets you link a provider that is not on its list. Many teams work this way, and it can be enough for one channel.

A Conversions API connection sends your events to the platform. It is not a measurement partnership, and the tool does not appear in the platform's partner program.

## What is the risk of measuring outside these programs?

The risk is not that events stop flowing. It is that the numbers you act on can be wrong in ways you do not see:

- **Missing conversions.** Without a self-attributing integration, the tool cannot receive the platform's touchpoint data. Installs that Google, Meta or TikTok drove can show up as organic, and those channels look weaker than they are.
- **Double-counted conversions.** If you add up each platform's own reports, the same install can be counted more than once. The total then looks larger than your real growth, and some channels look stronger than they are.
- **Weaker signals.** Ad platforms learn whom to target from the conversions you send back. Incomplete or misattributed postbacks give them less to learn from.

Each of these can move budget away from the channels that work. If this happens, it does not show up as an error. It shows up as ad spend that did less than your report said.

## Do you need an official MMP?

| Your situation | What usually fits |
|---|---|
| One ad channel, small budget | The platform's own reporting can be enough |
| Two or more ad channels | An MMP, so that one conversion is counted once |
| iOS campaigns on several channels | An MMP that supports SKAdNetwork for each channel is worth considering |
| Budget decisions based on revenue or retention by channel | An MMP that is in the programs of the platforms you buy from |

## What does Airbridge offer as an official MMP?

**In the ad platforms' partner programs**

- Google: Airbridge is on the [App Attribution Partner list](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12961402).
- Meta: Airbridge is a Meta Business Partner with badges for mobile measurement and multi-touch attribution (since 2021) and marketing mix modeling (since 2023).
- TikTok: Airbridge's [profile in TikTok's Marketing Partners directory](https://partners.tiktok.com/partner-details/7360566154416357377/pc/en) shows the Measurement category and the Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) specialty.
- Pinterest: [Pinterest's help center](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/third-party-partner-integration-set-up-options) lists Airbridge among its Mobile Measurement Partners.

**Connected to the channels you buy from**

- Six self-attributing networks: Google Ads, Meta Ads, Apple Ads and TikTok For Business on every plan, plus Amazon Ads and Petal Ads on the Growth Plan.
- More than 330 ad networks on the Growth Plan.

**Control over the signals you send**

- Postback rules for each channel, as described above.
- Signal Hold, in beta for Meta Ads. It holds a conversion postback, such as a purchase or a trial start, for a window you set, up to 24 hours. If a matching cancellation arrives in that window, neither event is sent. Meta then receives only the conversions that were not cancelled.

**More than attribution in one tool**

- Deep linking and web-to-app attribution.
- SKAdNetwork reporting and a conversion value manager.
- Revenue, retention, funnel and cohort reports, with predictive LTV (an estimate of how much revenue a user will bring).
- Pilot, an AI assistant, and an MCP server that lets AI tools such as Claude read your Airbridge data. Both are on every plan, with a monthly Pilot call limit on Core.

**A price that fits early-stage teams**

| | Core Plan | Growth Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Price | From $40 per month, 30-day free trial | Custom |
| Contract | No annual contract, cancel anytime | Through sales |
| Ad channels | Google, Meta, Apple Ads, TikTok | 330+ networks |
| Usage | 500K data points included, then $0.0001 each | Volume-based |
| Added in Growth | | Conversions API, fraud detection, custom events, raw data export, a dedicated customer success manager |

See the full comparison on the [Airbridge pricing page](https://www.airbridge.io/en/pricing), and each integration guide in the [Airbridge Help Center](https://help.airbridge.io/en/guides/integrating-ad-channels).

## What should you ask an attribution vendor?

1. Which measurement program are you in on each platform I buy from? Send the link to the platform's own list.
2. Do you receive touchpoint data from Google, Meta, TikTok and Apple Ads, or only from your own tracking links?
3. Can I choose which events go to each channel, and under which conditions?
4. How do you remove duplicate conversions across channels?
5. Do you support SKAdNetwork for each of these platforms?

## What is the bottom line?

Your ad budget is only as good as the numbers behind it. Check that your attribution tool is on the ad platforms' own partner lists, not only on its own website. Airbridge is on Google's App Attribution Partner list, holds Meta Business Partner measurement badges and is a Mobile Measurement Partner in TikTok's partner directory, and you can [try it free for 30 days](https://www.airbridge.io/en/pricing) on the Core Plan.

## FAQ

**What is an official MMP?**
An official MMP is a mobile measurement partner that an ad platform lists in its own measurement partner program. On Google, that program is App Attribution Partner. Google's list names Adjust, Airbridge, AppsFlyer, Branch, Kochava, Singular and Tenjin as of November 11, 2026.

**Is "Google Partner" the same as "App Attribution Partner"?**
No. Google Partner is a program for companies that manage Google Ads accounts. App Attribution Partner is Google's certification for app measurement tools.

**Is a Meta Tech Provider an official MMP?**
No. Tech Provider is Meta's term for a business whose app needs access to data that other businesses own on Meta. It requires business verification and app review. It is not a badge or a measurement partner program.

**Does a Google Partner badge mean a tool is certified for attribution?**
No. The Google Partner badge is for companies that manage Google Ads accounts. Its requirements are about ad spend, optimization score and Google Ads certifications. Google's certification for attribution tools is App Attribution Partner.

**What is the risk of using an attribution tool that is not an official MMP?**
Events can still reach the ad platforms, but the numbers you act on can be wrong. The tool may miss conversions that the platforms attributed, leave the same install claimed by more than one platform, or send weaker signals for optimization. Any of these can move budget away from the channels that work.

**How do I check if an attribution tool is an official MMP?**
Search for the tool in the ad platform's own partner list, such as Google's App Attribution Partner page. If the tool is not on the list, it does not hold that certification.

**Is Airbridge an official MMP?**
Yes. Airbridge is on Google's App Attribution Partner list, is a Mobile Measurement Partner in TikTok's Marketing Partners directory, and Pinterest's help center names Airbridge among the mobile measurement partners it supports. Airbridge also holds Meta Business Partner badges for mobile measurement, multi-touch attribution and marketing mix modeling.

**Can I run Google App campaigns without an official MMP?**
Yes. You can measure with Google's own tools. An MMP helps when you want one tool to measure Google next to your other channels with the same rules.

**Why do my ad platform numbers differ from my MMP?**
Each platform counts the conversions it claims, with its own conversion window. An MMP applies one rule to all channels and removes duplicates. Some difference is normal. Aligned conversion windows reduce it.

**How much does an official MMP cost?**
Prices vary by vendor and volume. Airbridge's Core Plan starts at $40 per month with a 30-day free trial and no annual contract.

## You can now measure app installs and purchases from ChatGPT Ads with Airbridge

URL: https://www.airbridge.io/en/blog/chatgpt-ads-integration
Language: English
Published: 2026-11-06
Author: Team Airbridge

On October 5, 2026, OpenAI [announced new measurement capabilities and an expanded partner ecosystem for ChatGPT Ads](https://openai.com/index/new-chatgpt-ads-format-and-measurement/). **Airbridge is one of the attribution partners OpenAI named.**

[Measurement partner logos for ChatGPT Ads announced by OpenAI]

With Airbridge, you can measure whether users who came through ChatGPT Ads installed your app, signed up, or made a purchase. You can also send the app events you need to ChatGPT Ads via postback and use them for campaign optimization.

When you test a new ad channel, you need to compare its install and purchase performance with your existing channels, and also prepare the settings for sending conversion data to the channel. In this post, we’ll walk you through how measurement works between ChatGPT Ads and Airbridge, the integration steps, and what to check during setup.

**📌 Key takeaways**

- **Measure installs, sign-ups, and purchases.** Use Airbridge to measure traffic from ChatGPT Ads and in-app conversions. When you compare performance with your existing ad channels, check the attribution window of each channel.
- **Send the conversion data you need to ChatGPT Ads.** Send app events such as installs, sign-ups, and purchases via postback and use them for campaign optimization.
- **Set up postbacks first, then use your tracking link.** Data collected before postbacks are set up is not sent to ChatGPT Ads. In Ads Manager Beta, enter the part of the tracking link up to and including the ?, followed by tracking_template_id, in [Default Ad Destination URL], and the remaining parameters in [Tracking parameters].

## How is ChatGPT Ads performance measured?

According to OpenAI, ads don’t influence ChatGPT’s answers and are displayed separately from them, and users’ conversations are kept private from advertisers.

To check whether users who came through ChatGPT Ads went on to install or purchase, you need to collect conversion data. When you send this data to ChatGPT Ads, you can use it for campaign optimization. When you compare performance with other ad channels, you also need to check the attribution criteria of each channel.

### 1. App events are sent via postback

In apps, the Airbridge SDK collects events such as installs, sign-ups, and purchases, and Airbridge sends the collected events to ChatGPT Ads through the Conversions API (CAPI). You don’t need to add a web pixel to your app. Here’s how a web pixel differs from the Conversions API, a server-to-server method.

- **Web pixel:** Code installed on a web page that sends visitors’ behavioral data to the ad channel.
- **Conversions API:** A method of sending conversion data from the advertiser’s server to the ad channel’s server.

[**OpenAI explains that**](https://ads.openai.com/blog/more-ways-to-measure) advertisers can send conversion data through the pixel and the Conversions API and use it for campaign optimization.

### 2. To compare ad channels, you need a common attribution standard

Each channel’s report **counts performance based on the attribution window and method set by that channel**. So if you compare the numbers from ChatGPT Ads and your existing ad channels as they are, you may end up evaluating the same purchase journey by different standards.

For example, let’s say a user clicks a search ad, then clicks a ChatGPT ad and installs your app. If each channel credits the install based on its own attribution criteria, the same install can be included in both reports. To decide which channel should get more budget, you need to compare performance by a common attribution standard.

Based on the ad touchpoints and install data it collects, Airbridge determines which channel contributed to the install according to defined rules such as attribution windows and touchpoint priority. Instead of adding up the installs in each channel’s report, you can compare channel performance based on the attribution results determined by Airbridge. In addition, sending conversion data such as installs and purchases to the channels lets you use it for campaign optimization.

When you test a new channel, prepare these two things.

1. **Performance comparison standard:** Attribution rules for comparing install and purchase performance across channels
2. **Conversion data delivery:** Settings for sending measured app events to the ad channel

## What changes when you connect with Airbridge?

With Airbridge, you can **measure traffic from ChatGPT Ads with tracking links and send app conversion data to ChatGPT Ads via postback**. In other words, you measure the behavior of users who came through your ads and use that data for campaign optimization as well.

### 1. Set the attribution windows to compare with your existing ad channels

To compare the installs and purchases attributed to ChatGPT Ads with your existing ad channels, you need to check which period of touchpoints and conversions each channel counts as performance.

In Airbridge, you can set the following two windows in the **[Attribution Rule] tab under [Integrations] → [Ad Channel Integration] → [ChatGPT Ads]**.

1. **Lookback window:** The period before a target event, such as an install, within which ad touchpoints are considered for attribution.
2. **Attribution window:** The period after a target event within which subsequent events are linked to that attribution.

Performance numbers for each channel can vary depending on the windows applied. Check which windows are applied to ChatGPT Ads and your existing channels so you know why the numbers differ.

👉 [Airbridge Lookback and Attribution Window Setup guide](https://help.airbridge.io/en/guides/setting-attribution-window)

If you work with an agency, **also grant it access to this channel’s data in the [Agency Settings] tab**.

### 2. Send install, sign-up, and purchase data to ChatGPT Ads

App events measured by Airbridge can be **sent to ChatGPT Ads via postback and used for campaign optimization**.
